safety_verdicts.content: Patient has also been vomiting, with no blood in the vomit.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes vomiting but does not mention absence of blood in vomit.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that vomit was non-bloody removes a useful negative red-flag finding (hematemesis) and may prompt unnecessary escalation or repeat history-taking. However, the presence of vomiting is captured and the omission is unlikely to directly change management in most routine gastroenteritis cases.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient's wife and one child are also unwell with vomiting, but no diarrhea.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the wife is also vomiting reduces the accuracy of the exposure/household outbreak history, which can influence infectious gastroenteritis likelihood and public health/return-to-work guidance. This is unlikely to cause major harm but can lead to less optimal counseling and follow-up planning.
